title: More sellers join

predict.q: A market has 2 sellers. 4 more join. What happens to the market price?

options.s: It rises, because more sellers means more demand
options.fb: Demand comes from buyers. New sellers add to supply, not demand.

options.s: It falls, because supply shifts right
options.fb: More sellers offer more at every price, so supply shifts right: the price falls from £16 to £9 and each seller sells less (28 → 14).

options.s: It stays the same, because demand has not changed
options.fb: Demand is unchanged, but supply has increased, so the old price leaves a surplus and falls.

options.s: It falls, because demand shifts left
options.fb: Price does fall, but because supply rises. Market demand has not changed; it is shared among more sellers.

task: Move the "number of sellers" slider from 2 to 6, then on to 10, and watch the supply curve, the price and the sales of each seller.

target.do: Move the number of sellers slider from 2 to 6, then press Check.

takeaway: More sellers shift supply right; the price falls and each seller sells less, so profits fall.
